result.rationale: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response (new file: `const response = await fetch(...); return response;`). Google's CalendarService then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` — a fetch Response has no `data` property, so token is undefined and this throws (or writes corrupt data), and the result is persisted via prisma.credential.update. The diff confirms the sync branch never parses the response body, so the described mechanism is accurate.

judged_text: In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the code immediately reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, which is undefined on a Response — the sync contract ("response should only contain the access token and expiry date") is never actually parsed from the Response body. With credential sync enabled, every Google calendar operation after token expiry sets googleCredentials.access_token to undefined and writes a broken key to prisma.credential, permanently corrupting the stored credential; zero tests in this diff cover the credential-sync branch of refreshOAuthTokens, so this data-corruption path is completely unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In the new sync branch, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`, i.e. a `Response` object (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). But callers like Google Calendar still treat the return as an axios/google-auth style object: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`). A `Response` has no `.data`, so in credential-sync mode `token` will be `undefined` (or will throw when reading `token.access_token`), meaning the sync response is never parsed/used. This is a concrete behavioral break introduced by the diff. (The finding's “writes a broken key” part is less directly shown because the code may throw before the Prisma update, but the core incompatibility/incorrect parsing is verifiable.)
